entries.title: A closed Call for Reviewers no longer takes invites or imports
entries.summary: **Invite** and **Import** are disabled on a closed call, or one past its closing date, with a note saying what to change: reopen the call, or move the closing date later in **Settings**. The server refuses the same additions, so nobody lands on a call that has stopped taking people.

where.path: Program → Evaluation → Call for reviewers → call; Awards → program → Call for reviewers → call

entries.use_case: A program chair who closed the call last week can't accidentally invite another reviewer into it; the page tells them to reopen it or extend the deadline first.

cs_action.note: Nothing to enable. Customers who want late additions reopen the call or move its closing date in Settings.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why Invite or Import is greyed out on a call, or wants to add reviewers after the deadline.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer running a Call for Reviewers on Sessions or Awards.

entries.title: Re-approve someone you declined on a Call for Reviewers
entries.summary: People an admin declined can be **Approved** again from the people list. People who declined their own invitation stay declined, and the row says to remove them before inviting them again. The reviewer portal now shows the matching message for each case.

where.path: Program → Evaluation → Call for reviewers → call → people list; Awards → program → Call for reviewers → call → people list; reviewer portal

entries.use_case: An organizer who declined a reviewer by mistake, or changed their mind once the pool looked thin, can approve that person again in one click instead of re-inviting them.

cs_action.note: A self-declined person can't be approved: remove them from the call, then invite them again.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer declined a reviewer by mistake or needs to grow a thin reviewer pool late.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Require approval on a Call for Reviewers.

entries.title: Call for Reviewers expertise: dropdown session fields, Awards nomination fields and nested sub-topics
entries.summary: Expertise on a Sessions call can use the event's **dropdown** session fields, and those answers count toward **Match expertise** on Assignments. In Awards, a nomination field's menu gains **Offer to reviewers as expertise** (shown as a **Reviewer expertise** badge, and kept when the program is duplicated). Sub-topics now sit under their parent topic in the admin picker and on the reviewer's interest form.

where.path: Program → Evaluation → Call for reviewers → Create / Settings → Expertise; Awards → program → Edit → nomination form → field menu; reviewer interest form

entries.use_case: A medical meeting that tags sessions with a Specialty dropdown can ask reviewers for the same specialty and have Match expertise pair them, and an awards program can let reviewers pick from the categories its nominees already choose.

cs_action.note: Customers who couldn't find their session fields in the Expertise picker: only dropdown (single or multi-select) fields with options are offered; text, number and contact fields are not.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Call for Reviewers setup calls, and any customer whose session or nomination categories should drive reviewer matching.
internal.who_should_get_it: Medical and scientific meetings with specialty or track dropdowns, and Awards customers with category-style nomination fields.

entries.title: Evaluation plan wizard no longer reports unsaved changes on open
entries.summary: Opening a saved evaluation plan no longer shows **Has unsaved changes** before you've touched anything. The **Assignments** step has a roomier layout, so the reviewer, matching and preview columns no longer crowd each other.

where.path: Program → Evaluation → plan → Edit → Assignments

entries.use_case: Program teams stop getting a leave-page warning on a plan they only opened to look at, and can read the Assignments step without squinting.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reported a leave-page warning on an evaluation plan they had not edited.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer building evaluation plans in Sessions 2.0.

entries.title: Messages menu: conversations get their own inbox, separate from the notification bell
entries.summary: A **Messages** icon beside the bell collects every thread, note and @mention you are part of, with a **Threads** tab (one row per conversation, unread count, **Mentioned you**) and a **Notes & mentions** tab. The bell now holds everything else, and **See all messages** opens a full page with an **Open** / **Resolved** filter.

where.path: Header → Messages (speech-bubble icon beside the bell); Event or Organization → Messages page

entries.use_case: A program manager answering speakers no longer has to dig replies out from under submission and export alerts: every open conversation is one click away, with the ones that @mention them flagged.

cs_action.note: Appears automatically for organizations with Notifications on. Message and mention notifications moved out of the bell into Messages, so the bell count drops for active messaging users — expect a "where did my notifications go" question.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Customers who message speakers, reviewers or sponsors inside Sessionboard, or who complain that replies get lost in the bell.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every organization using Notifications and record messaging; most useful to teams running reviewer or speaker threads across several events.
internal.gotchas: The badge counts unread threads plus unread notes & mentions for the current event; All events widens the list, not the badge. Threads with no messages are hidden. Mark all read clears both tabs but leaves the bell untouched.
internal.talk_track: Messages is your conversation inbox; the bell is for everything that happened. Nothing shows up in both.

entries.title: Disclosures: collect financial-relationship and conflict-of-interest forms by private link
entries.summary: **Disclosures** is a new Early Access **Preview**. Build a form from a template (**ACCME standard financial disclosure**, **Simple conflict of interest**, **Reviewer / committee conflict of interest**, or from scratch), send it from a contact's **Disclosure** tab, a bulk selection, or the **Requests** tab, and the person completes it from a private single-use link with no login and nothing on file revealed. Every contact shows **Current**, **Expiring**, **Expired** or **Missing**, with a **Disclosure** column on contact lists; a submission form can collect disclosures from its participants on the way in.

enable.path: Early Access → Preview → Disclosures

where.path: CRM → Disclosures; contact profile → Disclosure tab; Contacts list → bulk actions → Send Disclosure Request

entries.use_case: A CME coordinator who used to email a PDF disclosure to every faculty member and track replies in a spreadsheet sends one request from the speaker list, sees who is current at a glance, and never asks someone who disclosed six months ago to do it again.

cs_action.note: Medical/scientific and association customers running accredited CE, or anyone collecting reviewer or judge COI by email today. It does not need Lessons & Credits — turn the Preview on for them from Early Access or walk them through it.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any mention of ACCME, COI, faculty disclosure, reviewer conflicts, or 'we chase speakers for a form every year'.
internal.who_should_get_it: Medical and scientific conferences, associations with awards or abstract review, and any customer who asked for disclosure tracking.
internal.gotchas: Org-wide Preview; the Disclosures page is under CRM at the organization level (no event sidebar entry yet — event contacts still get the tab, column and bulk send). A role needs the new Disclosures permissions to create forms or send; on an environment where the permission seed has not run the tabs say "You don't have access". Links expire after 30 days by default and are single-use; the recipient never sees prior answers.

entries.title: Pathways: plain menu labels, a setup-first Overview, and one place to connect HubSpot or Salesforce
entries.summary: The Pathways menu now says what each page does: **Feedback** (Pre-event quiz, Surveys), **Results** (Topics, Attendees, **Program report** — formerly *The loop*), **Outreach**, and **Data** (**HubSpot**, Salesforce, **Membership & pipeline**). **Overview** opens on the setup checklist until the connections are in place, each check shows an error and a **Retry** if it cannot load, the Topics and Attendee directories use the same selectable table as **CRM → Accounts**, and HubSpot and Salesforce are installed from **Apps** like every other connector.

enable.path: Early Access → Preview → Pathways

where.path: Event or Organization → Pathways (Feedback, Results, Outreach, Data); Organization → Apps → HubSpot / Salesforce

entries.use_case: A program manager trying Pathways for the first time lands on a checklist that says what to connect and why, and finds the pre-event quiz, the attendance results and the HubSpot connection under names that mean something without a tour.

cs_action.note: Preview feature; relabels only. Anyone who learned the earlier names (Listen / Program / Activate, The loop, Shape the program, HubSpot sync, Value data) will find the same pages under the new ones.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Pathways preview customers who asked where the quiz or the HubSpot connection lives, or who saw an empty Overview before connecting anything.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every organization with the Pathways preview on; nothing to do for the rest.
internal.staff_path: Early Access → Preview → Pathways; staff-only prototype items no longer render an empty group header for customers.
internal.gotchas: The pre-event quiz is called Program Pulse in the Help Center and Pre-event quiz in the menu. Program report is the page the attendance guide used to call The loop.
internal.talk_track: Same Pathways, plainer signposts: Feedback is what people tell you, Results is what the program did, Outreach is what you send, Data is what it is connected to.

entries.title: Clips you just exported show up at once — rendering, failed, and where they came from
entries.summary: **Media → Clips** now lists a clip the moment you click **Export**: the card reads **Rendering…**, turns playable on its own, and a render that could not finish shows **Export failed** with the reason instead of vanishing. Each card names the recording it was cut from and links back to it. The **All / AI / Yours / Imported** tabs filter real clips, not only demo data.

enable.path: Early Access → Preview → Marketing (Clips)

where.path: Marketing → Media → Clips

entries.use_case: A marketer exports three clips before a meeting and can see all three rendering in the library, instead of refreshing an empty tab and exporting them again.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says a clip they exported 'never showed up', or asks which recording a clip came from.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone on the Marketing preview who cuts clips.
internal.gotchas: A clip that fails stays in the library marked failed with its reason; delete it from the card if it should not linger. Dispatch and Market pickers still list only playable clips.

entries.title: Deleted clips go to Trash and can be restored
entries.summary: Deleting a clip no longer makes it disappear for good. It lands in **Media → Library → Trash** next to deleted recordings, with the date, and **Restore** puts it back in the clips library.

enable.path: Early Access → Preview → Marketing (Clips)

where.path: Marketing → Media → Library → Trash

entries.use_case: Someone deletes the wrong clip the night before a campaign and gets it back in one click, caption styling and all.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks where a deleted clip went, or whether Delete on a clip is permanent.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone on the Marketing preview.

entries.title: An uploaded SRT or VTT becomes the recording's transcript
entries.summary: Upload a recording, then its captions with the same file name (`keynote.mp4` → `keynote.srt`), and the captions are written in as that recording's transcript — no transcription run, and no stray item in the Library. Previously a caption file was treated as a video and the import failed. Audio-only uploads are also filed as audio now.

enable.path: Early Access → Preview → Marketing

where.path: Marketing → Media → Import

entries.use_case: A society that already paid for human-made captions keeps them, instead of paying for a second machine transcript that is less accurate.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer has caption files from their AV vendor or webinar platform and asks whether to upload them.
internal.who_should_get_it: Medical and scientific programs with vendor captions; anyone importing a webinar archive that came with .srt files.
internal.gotchas: Upload the recording before the captions — the match is by file name against recordings already uploaded. A caption file with no matching recording is refused with a message saying so.

entries.title: The 10-minute cap for re-encoded clips is shown before you export
entries.summary: Clips with captions, a 9:16 or 1:1 crop, an animated style or overlays are re-encoded and capped at **10 minutes**. The editor now says so up front: **Export** is disabled with the reason when a trimmed window or a timeline selection is longer, and a plain trim — **Original** with **No captions** — is called out as having no limit. The Import tab states the upload limits (50 GB per file, about six hours) in the same place you drop files.

enable.path: Early Access → Preview → Marketing (Clips)

where.path: Marketing → Media → recording → Edit & clip → Suggested clips / Clip selection; Media → Import

entries.use_case: An organizer trimming a 14-minute panel highlight finds out before exporting that captions push it over the cap, and either shortens it or exports it plain — instead of waiting on a render that fails.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports an export that 'just failed' on a long clip, or asks how long a clip can be.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone on the Marketing preview who cuts clips.

entries.title: Content Gallery Sites can be found by search engines
entries.summary: A published gallery that is not **Private** is now indexable: its Hub, Explore, collection and item pages are crawlable, listed in the Site's sitemap, and served to crawlers instead of being blocked. **Hide from search engines** (Design tab) still adds `noindex` to the whole gallery and drops it from the sitemap. Previously every gallery page was marked noindex and crawlers received a 403, so no gallery could rank.

enable.path: Early Access → Preview → Content Galleries

where.path: Gallery → Design → Search engines; the gallery's public Site

entries.use_case: A society's on-demand library and session catalog start appearing in Google for the talks and speakers in them, which is most of the point of publishing one.

cs_action.note: Galleries that were published before this change are now indexable unless Private. Check email-gated, members-only and SSO galleries with the customer and turn on Hide from search engines where they expect privacy. Locked items and My list are never indexed either way.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why their gallery does not show up in Google, or wants to make sure a gated one does not.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every published Session Catalog / On-Demand Hub; review with any customer running an email-gated or members-only gallery.
internal.gotchas: The crawler-facing half runs in the sites.sessionboard.com edge Worker (lennd/cloudlfare-workers#11), deployed 2026-10-10; it is not tracked by the deploy workflows listed here. Indexing by Google itself takes days to weeks after the pages become crawlable.

entries.title: Embargoed speakers and tags no longer leak through Explore filters
entries.summary: When an embargo withholds **Speakers** or **Tags**, those values now stay out of the Explore filter rail, its counts, search and the public feed until the lift. Before, the cards hid them but the filters still listed every withheld speaker and topic, so a visitor could find an embargoed talk by filtering for its presenter.

enable.path: Early Access → Preview → Content Galleries

where.path: Gallery → Access → Embargo → What to withhold; the public Explore page

entries.use_case: A scientific meeting under a press embargo can publish its catalog early without the filter rail giving away who is presenting what.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any scientific or medical program using embargoes; a customer asking whether the catalog is 'safe' to publish before the meeting.
internal.who_should_get_it: Medical and scientific programs with embargoed abstracts.

entries.title: Manage attendee consent, data export, and deletion from Person 360
entries.summary: The **Person 360** header now shows a consent badge (**Given**, **Withdrawn**, or **Not recorded**) and a privacy menu with three actions: **Export data** (downloads the person's data as JSON), **Mark consent given / withdrawn / Clear consent**, and **Delete attendee** (with a confirmation dialog explaining what is removed and what is kept). A notice appears on the page when consent is withdrawn or when org-level data processing is off, and each registration record shows **consent withdrawn** where applicable. A new **Pathways data** page under **Org Settings** adds a **Process attendee data** toggle and guidance on handling attendee data requests.

enable.path: Org Settings → Pathways data → Process attendee data

where.path: Pathways → People → [person] (Person 360 header); Org Settings → Pathways data

entries.use_case: Organizers who need to honour attendee data-access or deletion requests (e.g. GDPR or CCPA) can now export a person's data, record or clear their consent, or permanently remove their attendee records — all from the Person 360 page, without needing a support ticket. The org-level processing toggle lets privacy-conscious teams pause data processing across all attendees at once.

cs_action.note: The delete action is irreversible — attendee records, activity, and linked survey answers are removed permanently. Confirm the customer understands what stays (event totals, the Speaker CRM contact) before they use it in production.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to handle a GDPR/CCPA deletion or data-access request, or when they want to track attendee consent status.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Pathways (beta) who collects attendee registrations and needs to demonstrate privacy compliance.
internal.gotchas: es/de/fr translations of the new copy are not yet written — UI falls back to English for those locales. No browser QA against a live API has been completed yet. The legacy AttendeeDrawer (demo only) is unchanged.
internal.talk_track: If an attendee asks you to delete their data or export what you hold on them, you can do that in seconds from their Person 360 page — no back-end work needed. You can also record whether they gave consent and pause all attendee data processing org-wide from Org Settings.

draft.docs_gap: No guide covers the Pathways Person 360 privacy controls (consent badge, data export, delete attendee) or the Org Settings → Pathways data processing switch; a new article should document these privacy and data-management actions and their permission requirements.
permissions_to_confirm: Contacts READ + EXPORT — required for Export data
Contacts UPDATE — required for consent actions
Contacts DELETE — required for Delete attendee

entries.title: Program Pulse: build and publish a live attendee quiz with Session Picks
entries.summary: Organizers can now use **Program Pulse** (found under Pathways → Pulse) to build a real quiz in **Studio**, publish it, and share a public link or iframe embed. Attendees answer topic questions at `/pulse/:token` with no login required, optionally leave an email for personalised picks, and see session recommendations from the engine. The **Session Picks** widget at `/pulse/:token/picks` can be iframed anywhere; it shows personal picks for someone who took the quiz on that device, or general picks for everyone else. **Results** shows finished responses, channel breakdown, topic demand vs. programme sessions, per-question counts, and a CSV download of picks per attendee — with honest empty states when no answers have come in yet.

enable.path: Pathways → Pulse

where.path: Pathways → Pulse → Studio / Results; public quiz at /pulse/:token; Session Picks widget at /pulse/:token/picks

entries.use_case: An organizer can launch a short topic quiz before or during the event, let attendees answer on their own device with no account needed, and immediately see which topics have the most demand versus what is already on the programme. Attendees get personalised session recommendations the moment they finish.

cs_action.note: The API integration is covered by server-side tests but the UI has not been clicked through against a live API in a browser; validate end-to-end in staging before enabling for customers. The de, es, and fr locales fall back to English. match_reason text comes from the API in English only.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to help attendees discover relevant sessions, or wants to measure topic demand before finalising the programme.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events on the Pathways beta that want attendee-facing session discovery or pre-event topic research.
internal.gotchas: Admins can reword quiz screens but cannot add or reorder them. The ?channel= parameter must be added manually to share links for Results to separate traffic sources. No persona or destinations panel yet (PLS-007). Embed is iframe-only; no embed script.
internal.talk_track: Program Pulse turns your taxonomy into a short quiz attendees can take on any device — no login — and the engine recommends sessions that match their interests. You see exactly which topics are in demand versus what you have already scheduled, and can download a per-attendee picks CSV for follow-up.

draft.docs_gap: No guide covers Program Pulse (the live quiz, Session Picks widget, or Studio); a new article should document how to build and publish a Pulse quiz, share the embed snippets, read Results, and embed the Session Picks widget.

entries.title: Manage attendee consent, export personal data, and delete attendee records in Pathways
entries.summary: Organizers can now record and update an attendee's consent state (**Granted**, **Withdrawn**, or **Unknown**) directly on their Pathways person record. A **Withdrawn** consent stops new attendee signals from being collected and parks the person's identifiers so they are not re-created on re-sync. A full data export (JSON) is available per person, covering their attendee records, signals, survey responses, and learning data. A hard-delete removes the person's signals, survey data, and attendee rows in one transaction and permanently suppresses their identifiers. A new org-level **Processing Enabled** toggle in Pathways settings lets organizers turn off all attendee-signal processing — including Speaker Score attendee ratings, portal feedback, and person-merge — while keeping the roster sync running.

where.path: Pathways → People → [person] → Consent; Pathways → Settings

entries.use_case: If an attendee asks to have their data removed or withdraws consent under your privacy policy, you can update their consent state to stop new data collection immediately, export everything held about them for your records, and then permanently delete their data — all without leaving Sessionboard. The org-level processing toggle lets you pause all attendee-signal analysis for an event while still keeping the registration roster in sync.

cs_action.note: The PATHWAYS_SUPPRESSION_PEPPER env var must be set in Doppler before deploy; rotating it orphans all existing suppressions. Confirm with engineering that it is set permanently before any customer uses deletion or consent withdrawal.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about GDPR/CCPA compliance workflows, right-to-erasure requests, or wants to pause attendee analytics without stopping registration sync.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer on the Pathways beta who handles attendee PII or operates under privacy regulations requiring consent tracking and data deletion.
internal.staff_path: Pathways → People → [person record] for consent/export/delete; Pathways → Settings for the processing toggle
internal.gotchas: Aggregate tables (e.g. session fill counts) are not recomputed at delete time — they update on their next scheduled refresh. Signals collected before a withdrawal remain readable until the person is deleted; withdrawal stops new data only. After an org merge, suppressions from the source org do not carry over to the surviving org. The attendee-value layer (PR #4421) must also be merged and extended before value rows are included in exports and cleared on delete.
internal.talk_track: Sessionboard now gives you a full privacy workflow inside Pathways: mark consent, pull a data export for your records, and delete the person's data in one action — with suppression so they aren't accidentally re-created on the next registration sync.

draft.docs_gap: The Pathways guide (services/pathways/README.md exists internally but no public article covers Pathways consent management, data export, deletion, or the processing-enabled setting; a new article should document how organizers view and update an attendee's consent state, export their data, delete them, and toggle Pathways processing on or off at the org level.
permissions_to_confirm: Contacts READ + EXPORT or MANAGE (data export)

entries.title: Pathways surfaces now show live likely-audience data across sessions, agenda, CFP, Scout, speaker home, and portfolio
entries.summary: When the Pathways feature is enabled and an event has attendee history, six surfaces update with real audience data: the Sessions table gains a **Likely audience** column (removable via **Columns**); the **Agenda room fit** panel shows a likely-audience chip and an updated room-fit tooltip per session; the **Evaluation audience fit** panel ranks sessions by fit score and flags thin topics; the **Scout → From your audience** card lists audience gaps with past speakers per topic (requires Contacts READ permission); the **Know Your Room** card on the speaker home shows registered, likely, returning, and expected counts plus followed topics and rating track record; and the **Attendees → Portfolio** view adds an overlap matrix and topic coverage for upcoming events. Each surface shows a plain-language empty state when data is not yet available instead of sample data.

enable.path: Organization settings → Previews → Pathways

where.path: Sessions → table (Likely audience column); Agenda → room fit panel; Program → Evaluation → audience fit; Attendees → Scout → From your audience; Speaker home → Know Your Room card; Attendees → Portfolio

entries.use_case: Program teams with attendee history can now see which sessions are likely to draw the biggest crowds, spot topic gaps before the schedule is locked, and give speakers a realistic picture of their expected room — all without leaving Sessionboard.

cs_action.note: All surfaces are behind the Pathways flag; the flag must be on and the event must have attendee history for live data to appear. Demo mode still shows sample data for prospects.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to forecast session attendance, identify thin topics in their program, or give speakers pre-event room context.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on Pathways beta who have run at least one prior event with check-in or registration data in Sessionboard.
internal.gotchas: The Likely audience column only appears in the Sessions table once the event has attendee history; without history the column is not offered at all. Scout's From your audience card is hidden if the team member lacks Contacts READ. Know Your Room questions and clip reach have no live source yet and the card says so. Several sub-features (submitter track picker preview, Scout attendee practitioners, open-web finds) remain demo-only in this release.
internal.talk_track: With Pathways on, your program team can see a live likely-audience forecast on every session, rank CFP submissions by how well they fit your actual audience, and surface topic gaps — all driven by your real attendee history, not sample data.

draft.docs_gap: The session attendance and room fit guide should add a section explaining the Likely Audience column, the audience-fit ranking in CFP evaluation, the Scout 'From your audience' card, the Know Your Room card on the speaker home, and the Portfolio overlap matrix — all surfaces introduced by the Pathways likely-audience feature.
permissions_to_confirm: Contacts READ required for Scout → From your audience card

entries.title: Collect attendee topic interest before the event and surface personalised session picks with Program Pulse
entries.summary: A new **Pulse** survey type lets organizers publish a short pre-event quiz seeded from the event's own topics, formats and levels. Attendees answer anonymously or by email, and each person immediately receives a ranked list of **Session Picks** matched to their answers, past behaviour and session popularity. Admins can view response counts, per-question breakdowns and a **Topic Demand** panel that compares declared interest against past check-ins and the current programme, then export a **Picks CSV** (one row per pick per respondent) for deeper analysis.

enable.path: Pathways (must be enabled for the org)

where.path: Program → Pathways → Pulse

entries.use_case: Program teams running large conferences can gauge which topics, formats and levels have the most demand before the schedule is locked, and give each registered attendee a personalised shortlist of sessions to bookmark — all without requiring a login.

cs_action.note: Pathways must be enabled for the org before the Pulse tab appears. The UI PR (#945) must also be deployed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to validate topic demand before finalising the agenda, or wants to drive session discovery and pre-registration for attendees.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running multi-track conferences or summits who already use Pathways, or who are evaluating it; especially those who want pre-event engagement data.
internal.gotchas: Pulse surveys are hidden from the standard Program → Surveys list and from evaluation fill pages. The quiz is public (no login required) but rate-limited; a typed email cannot overwrite a completed response (returns 409). Signals are written to the attendee only if they did not untick consent and their record allows personalisation — otherwise signals are anonymous. Match reasons are English-only in this release. The picks CSV requires Contacts READ permission.
internal.talk_track: Before your event even opens, attendees tell you what they want to learn. Pulse turns those answers into a personalised session shortlist for each person and a topic-demand heatmap for your programme team — so you schedule with confidence and attendees show up to the right rooms.

draft.docs_gap: The /evaluations/surveys guide should add a section explaining Program Pulse (pulse surveys with kind='pulse'), covering how to create and publish a pulse, how attendees take the public quiz, how session picks are generated and displayed, and how admins read topic-demand results and export the picks CSV.
permissions_to_confirm: Contacts READ required to export the Picks CSV

entries.title: HubSpot connection page now shows live sync status, counts, and controls
entries.summary: The **Sessionboard in HubSpot** page (`/pathways/hubspot`) is now fully live. It shows how many people are eligible to be written to HubSpot (excluding those who withheld personalization consent), the number of matched HubSpot contacts and the match rate, companies rolled up, and when the last sync ran. Per-section toggles control **Contact properties**, **Company roll-up**, and **Create contacts for marketing opt-ins** (the last is disabled until **Contact properties** is on). **Sync now** and **Dry run** buttons are available when the connection is active and at least one section is enabled; the page polls every 5 seconds while a sync is running. Record errors from the last sync are listed per section, and a property reference explains which names, labels, and types are written to HubSpot.

enable.path: Apps → HubSpot

where.path: Pathways → Sessionboard in HubSpot

entries.use_case: Organizers who use HubSpot as their CRM can now see exactly how many contacts will be written, check the match rate, and control which data sections sync — without leaving Sessionboard. Running a dry run first lets them verify the output before committing a full sync.

cs_action.note: The processing gate (ATT-016) is a stub that always returns true; recommended-sessions properties 1–3 will be empty until the recommender is built. Confirm the org has HubSpot connected via Apps before walking them through the page.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how Sessionboard writes data to HubSpot or wants to audit what was synced last night.
internal.who_should_get_it: Orgs that have the Pathways beta enabled and have connected a HubSpot account.
internal.gotchas: If the org has CRM write-back disallowed, the page says so and sync controls are unavailable. Recommended sessions fields 1–3 will be empty until a future release. Consent withdrawal clears the corresponding HubSpot properties.
internal.talk_track: The new HubSpot page gives you a real-time view of your sync health — match rate, eligible contacts, last run status — and lets you toggle exactly which data sections flow into HubSpot. Use Dry run to preview before going live.

draft.docs_gap: The article index has no guide covering the HubSpot Pathways connection page; a new guide should document how to connect HubSpot, read sync counts and match rates, toggle per-section switches, run or dry-run a sync, and interpret record errors.

entries.title: Pathways data writes back to your organization's HubSpot portal
entries.summary: When the HubSpot integration is connected and Pathways is enabled, Sessionboard can push engagement data — top topics, engagement score, sessions attended, events attended, and recommended sessions — onto HubSpot contact and company records as custom `sb_*` properties. Enable the **Contacts** and **Companies** sections in **Apps → HubSpot → Settings**, then use **Sync now** to push immediately or let the nightly schedule run. A contact is created in HubSpot only when **Create contacts** is on and the person has opted in to marketing. If a person's `consent_personalization` flag is false, any previously written `sb_*` properties are cleared and the link is removed. All three settings default off.

enable.path: Apps → HubSpot → Settings → Contacts / Companies / Create contacts

where.path: Apps → HubSpot

entries.use_case: An event organizer who already uses HubSpot can automatically keep their CRM up to date with each attendee's topic interests and engagement score, so their marketing team can segment and follow up without any manual exports.

cs_action.note: All three write-back settings default off and require a HubSpot private-app token with the correct CRM scopes (crm.objects.contacts.read/write, crm.schemas.contacts.write, same for companies). internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to keep their HubSpot contact records enriched with Sessionboard engagement data without manual exports, or when they are already using the HubSpot contact pull and want to push data back.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who have HubSpot connected, use Pathways, and have a marketing team that segments by topic interest or engagement score.

Recommendations slots (sb_recommended_1–3) are created but never written until the Program Pulse ranker is on main. A missing private-app scope surfaces as a named error on the first sync run, not at connection time. The nightly push runs every ~20 hours per contact; manual 'Sync now' always writes regardless of the interval.
internal.talk_track: Sessionboard now writes your attendees' top topics, engagement scores, and attendance counts directly onto their HubSpot contact and company records as custom properties — so your marketing team always has fresh, event-driven data to segment on without touching a spreadsheet.

draft.docs_gap: The HubSpot integration guide should document the Pathways write-back feature: how to connect a private-app token, what the sb_* properties mean, how to enable the contacts and companies sections, what consent and marketing opt-in settings control, and how to read the sync status and error log.

entries.title: Community Roadmap now shows a Released column of shipped features

entries.title: See attendee account value across sessions, topics and person profiles

A value block (relationship, tier, money, account, renewal and read history) appears on the **Person** page only for team members who hold the per-person value permission; everyone else sees the block hidden. Rooms with fewer than 5 people display a suppression notice instead of individual data.

enable.path: Organization → Early Access → Pathways

where.path: Pathways → Settings → Value data; Event → Attendees → Value tab; Event → Attendees → Topics; Contacts → Person page

entries.title: Ideas board defaults to Open; status chips and category counts stay in sync with filters
entries.summary: The **Ideas** board now opens with **Open** selected by default so the most actionable ideas are visible immediately. The **Under Review** and **Shipped** chips now include all matching statuses (validating and under review; delivered, complete, and processed), so ideas that were previously missing from **Shipped** now appear. Category counts in the sidebar update to reflect the current status, search, and org filters — categories with no matches are dimmed rather than hidden, keeping the sidebar stable while filters load.

where.path: Community → Ideas

internal.talk_track: The Ideas board now opens on Open ideas by default, and every count you see — including the sidebar categories — reflects exactly what your current filters show.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the status chip order (Open first, All statuses last), the expanded status groupings for Under Review and Shipped, and how category counts dynamically reflect active filters.

entries.title: Ideas category counts now reflect active filters
entries.summary: The category list in the **Ideas** sidebar now shows counts that match whatever filters are active — status, search, or org scope — instead of static all-time totals. where.path: Community → Ideas → category sidebar

internal.talk_track: Category counts in the Ideas sidebar now stay in sync with whatever filters you have active, so the number you see is always the number you get.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document that category counts in the Ideas sidebar update dynamically to reflect active filters (status, search, org scope), not static post totals.

entries.title: Community's What's New and Roadmap now link to Help Center release notes
entries.summary: In **What's New**, each card title and **Read the release note** open the public Help Center release note, **How to use it** opens the customer guide, release dates show as days ago, and **All release notes** appears at the bottom. In **Roadmap**, Shipped cards show a **Release note ↗** link and the column footer shows "Newest 15 of N · All release notes"; ideas whose release is merged but not yet deployed carry a **Deploying soon** badge in the In Progress column. In the idea detail dialog, **Shipped in** lists the release notes that delivered the idea, or shows **Built and deploying soon** while staged.

where.path: Community → What's New; Community → Roadmap

entries.use_case: Organizers browsing What's New or the Roadmap can jump straight to the full Help Center release note or the relevant how-to guide without leaving the product, making it easier to act on new capabilities immediately.

entries.title: Send a $1.00 test charge to verify a payment gateway is fully configured
entries.summary: Each gateway row in Payment Settings now has a **Send $1.00 test charge** option. It tokenizes a card via Spreedly, runs a real authorization, and reports the outcome: approved and voided (with processor reference numbers), approved but void failed (so the admin knows a hold is outstanding), or declined with the raw gateway response and a provider-specific hint — for example, BluePay's **SECURITY ERROR** now surfaces a note to set **Hash Type in APIs** to **MD5** in the BluePay portal. The BluePay setup instructions also display this note before the first charge is attempted.

where.path: Awards → Payment Settings → gateway row menu → Send $1.00 test charge

entries.use_case: An organizer who just connected a BluePay (or any other) gateway can immediately confirm the credentials are fully correct — not just that the gateway saved — before any real submission fees are charged. If something is misconfigured, the declined result and the inline hint tell them exactly what to fix.

cs_action.note: Proactively share with any customer who has connected BluePay or reported mysterious SECURITY ERROR declines; the test charge will surface the MD5 hash-type misconfiguration immediately.

internal.when_to_bring_up: During gateway setup onboarding, or when a customer reports that Test Connection passed but live charges are failing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any Awards customer using BluePay (Fiserv) or any gateway where silent misconfiguration is possible.
internal.gotchas: The menu item only renders when the API returns a Spreedly environment_key (requires web-api #4407); on live gateways a real card will see a voided $1.00 authorization, so warn customers to use a card they control. If the void fails, a $1.00 hold will remain on the card until it expires.
internal.talk_track: You can now send a $1.00 test charge straight from the gateway row — it tells you exactly what went wrong if the gateway rejects it, including the specific fix for BluePay's hash-type setting.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the new "Send $1.00 test charge" menu action on each gateway row, explain the approved/voided, approved-but-void-failed, and declined result states, and note the BluePay "Hash Type in APIs" MD5 requirement surfaced by the hint text.

entries.title: Track session attendance, room fit, and speaker draw — and factor them into Speaker Score

where.path: Sessions → Session Fill; Sessions → Agenda → Room Fit; Org Settings → Speaker Score

entries.title: See the membership and pipeline value of every session's audience
entries.summary: Organizers can now import membership or CRM pipeline data and instantly see how many attendees in each session, topic, or speaker slot are existing members or customers — and what they are worth. Configure sources and field mappings under **Pathways → Settings → Value data**, then import a CSV or connect HubSpot, Salesforce, Nimble, or Fonteva. Each session, topic, and speaker card shows relationship breakdowns, tier counts, and pipeline totals per currency. Money and headcounts for rooms of fewer than five people are suppressed automatically. A new **View per-person pipeline and membership value** permission (Contacts) unlocks the individual-level drill-in and exact figures in small groups.

enable.path: Pathways (must be enabled for the org)

where.path: Pathways → Settings → Value data (configuration); Pathways → session / topic / speaker cards (rollup views)

Program teams can also use it to prioritise high-value topics and speakers when building the next agenda.

internal.who_should_get_it: Enterprise and association customers who have membership systems or CRM pipeline data and want to tie it to their program analytics.
internal.staff_path: Org settings → Early access / feature flags → Pathways

entries.title: Pathways: likely-audience estimates for topics and sessions
entries.summary: Pathways orgs now get a **Likely Audience** model that estimates how many attendees are likely to attend each topic and session, based on the org's own attendee history (up to 3 years of signals including registrations, attendance, ratings, surveys, and declared interests). Results include an **expected** headcount, a **confidence** level (`none` / `low` / `medium` / `high`), and a plain-language basis (e.g. "based on 1,240 attendees across 3 past events"). The model runs nightly and can be triggered on demand. Room-fit suggestions now incorporate likely-audience figures as a third predictor. A **Know Your Room** summary is available to speakers in Pathways orgs (super-user preview only). An org-level **gaps** view surfaces uncovered or thin topics and past speakers, and a **portfolio** view shows overlap, movers, and coverage across events.

enable.path: Org Settings → Early Access → Pathways

where.path: Pathways → Likely Audience (event and org views); Me → Know Your Room (speaker preview)

entries.use_case: Program teams can see which sessions and topics are likely to draw the biggest crowds before the agenda is finalised, so they can assign appropriately sized rooms and prioritise content gaps. Speakers in Pathways orgs get an aggregate view of their upcoming sessions' expected audience.

cs_action.note: Requires the Pathways flag to be on for the org. The /me/know-your-room speaker endpoint is additionally gated to super-user preview only.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to right-size rooms, reduce no-shows, or identify content gaps before the event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Pathways beta customers with at least one past event's worth of attendee history in Sessionboard.

draft.docs_gap: The room-fit guide should add a section explaining the new likely-audience predictor, how confidence levels are calculated, what the gaps and portfolio org-level views show, and how to trigger an on-demand refresh.

entries.title: Test a payment gateway with a real $1.00 charge, and payers now see plain-language error messages
entries.summary: A new **Send $1.00 test charge** action on a saved gateway runs an actual authorization against the processor and immediately voids it, confirming the gateway credentials work end-to-end. If the void fails, the admin is told a $1 hold may be outstanding. When a payment does fail at checkout, payers see a plain-language message (e.g. "Your card was declined") instead of raw gateway text like `SECURITY ERROR` or `Declined Sale`; the original gateway message is preserved in logs and on the payment record for support.

where.path: Organization → Payment Settings → Gateways → [gateway] → Send $1.00 test charge

entries.use_case: An organizer who just connected a BluePay or other gateway can immediately verify the credentials actually reach the processor — not just that Spreedly accepted the key shape — before any real submissions come in. Submitters who hit a genuine card decline see a helpful message rather than a cryptic gateway error code.

cs_action.note: Proactively reach out to any customer who has reported mysterious payment failures or SECURITY ERROR messages — the new test-charge action will confirm whether their gateway is misconfigured. BluePay customers specifically: check that Hash Type in APIs is set to MD5.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When onboarding a customer with a new payment gateway, or when a customer reports that payments are failing with no clear reason.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Awards or CFP with a paid submission tier, especially those on BluePay/Fiserv.
internal.gotchas: If the $1.00 void fails (e.g. on a live gateway with no void window), the auth is still reported as a success but voided: false is returned — the admin should be told a $1 hold may appear on the test card. The companion web-ui-v2 PR (UI button) is required for organizers to trigger this from the product; the API endpoint is live but the button may not be deployed yet.
internal.talk_track: You can now prove your gateway works before your call opens — just hit Send $1.00 test charge, enter a card, and we'll authorize and void a dollar against your live processor. If it fails, we'll tell you exactly what to fix, like switching BluePay's Hash Type to MD5.

draft.docs_gap: The BluePay setup section should note that Hash Type in APIs must be set to MD5 (not HMAC_SHA512) for Spreedly compatibility, and the guide should document the new Send $1.00 test charge action and what the voided/void_message response fields mean.

entries.title: Speaker portal now has a dedicated Feedback page

entries.title: Cvent syncs now stop cleanly on daily quota exhaustion and explain why in History

The evaluator review page surfaces a **Past attendee feedback** card under each named speaker. A new **Selection review** tab on the Eval Plan v2 detail page cross-references committee scores, prior attendee ratings, and delivered scores — including a "what to change next year" cut for tracks and formats where delivery missed the committee score by ≥ 1 star. Org-level settings under **Settings › Speaker Score** let admins configure score weights, recent-event doubling, minimum speaker ratings, and which native survey questions count as "Rates the speaker."

where.path: Contacts → contact profile (Speaker Score popover); Contacts → contact profile → Program tab; Program → Evaluation → plan → Selection review; Org Settings → Speaker Score

entries.title: Import past Cvent events and vendor survey results into a person's 360 profile
entries.summary: Two new capabilities for Cvent-connected organizations: (1) **Import Past Events** lets organizers queue historical Cvent events for backfill so that a person's 360 profile shows registrations and sessions from years before the current Sessionboard mapping. (2) Cvent session and speaker survey responses now sync into the **Surveys** tab on the 360, appearing as read-only **From Cvent** entries — native surveys remain fully editable and are unaffected.

where.path: Apps → Connections → [Cvent connection] → Attendees → Import Past Events; Person 360 → Surveys tab

entries.use_case: Organizations that have used Cvent for multiple years can now surface a speaker's or attendee's full history — past events and session ratings — directly on their Sessionboard 360 profile, without manual data entry. This gives program teams the attendance and performance context they need when evaluating returning speakers or building targeted outreach.

cs_action.note: Past-events backfill must be triggered per connection via the new Import Past Events UI (companion UI PR #893 required). Survey sync (syncSurveys) is off by default on the Cvent manifest and must be enabled per connection. The Cvent survey entity has not yet been live-verified against a real Cvent account — treat as provisional until Josh's live check is complete.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why their person 360 only shows events from the current Sessionboard mapping, or when they want session/speaker ratings from Cvent to appear in Sessionboard.

internal.staff_path: Apps → Connections → [Cvent connection] → Attendees page (Import Past Events dialog) and connection settings (syncSurveys toggle)
internal.gotchas: Cvent survey sync is NOT live-verified yet — do not promise accuracy until the live check passes. Vendor surveys are strictly read-only in the admin; any attempt to edit them will be blocked with a validation error. Past-event backfill skips remote events already mapped to a Sessionboard event.
internal.talk_track: With past-events backfill, your team can see every event a speaker attended in Cvent — not just the ones already mapped in Sessionboard — right on their 360 profile. And once survey sync is enabled, session and speaker ratings from Cvent flow in automatically, giving you a performance record across years.

draft.docs_gap: The Cvent integration guide should add sections covering: (1) how to queue and monitor a past-events backfill, (2) enabling survey sync and what the read-only From Cvent badge means on the Surveys tab, and (3) how past-event registrations and survey results appear on the Person 360.

entries.title: Team Lead can now summarise the Advocacy campaigns list pages

entries.title: Sync Doctor now surfaces SSO sign-in failures in the Open Issues view
entries.summary: SSO failures appear as rows in **Admin → Sync Doctor → Open Issues**, labelled **SSO · \<IdP\>** with a key icon. A **Syncs & SSO** filter (with **Syncs** and **SSO** sub-options) lets you narrow the list. Opening an SSO row shows a detail sheet with the failure message, stage, code, OAuth/IdP error, HTTP status, route, initiating party (SP or IdP), masked last user, and trace ID; for spike events, the email domains involved are listed. entries.title: Embed a Site form on any external web page with a single script tag
entries.summary: A new JavaScript loader (`sessionboard-form-embed.js`) lets you drop a Sessionboard Site form into any external web page using two lines of HTML. Add the `<script>` tag and a `<sessionboard-form src="…">` element pointing at your form's `/embed/` URL; the loader creates the iframe, adjusts its height automatically as the form grows, fires a `sessionboard:form-submitted` event on the page when the form is submitted, and redirects the top-level page on completion — no custom JavaScript required.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Embeds V2

where.path: Sites → your site → form page → share/embed URL

entries.use_case: An organizer who wants to collect CFP submissions or interest-form responses directly on their own conference website can paste two lines of HTML to embed the Sessionboard form inline — visitors never leave the page, and the organizer's site is notified the moment someone submits.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to put a submission or interest form on their own website without redirecting visitors to a Sessionboard-hosted URL.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who manage their own conference or association website and want a seamless on-site form experience.
internal.gotchas: The src attribute must be an https *.sessionboard.com URL containing /embed/ in the path; any other URL silently renders nothing. Redirect on submission only follows https URLs. All four companion PRs must be deployed together.

entries.title: Multiple reliability fixes: role deletion, portal login sharing, community opt-out, embed labels, and more

- **Deleting an org role** with a replacement no longer removes the role holders from the org; deleting without a replacement is now refused.
- **Share login details** bulk send no longer fails when a contact's portal login email differs from their current contact email — mismatched recipients are skipped and reported instead of failing the whole send.
- **Community email opt-out** now works: the notification types list accepts `scope=community` and community emails link to **Account** settings.
- **Embeds V2** legacy-fallback participant rows now show the correct role label (speaker, moderator, or chairperson) instead of a blank.
- **Team Lead** `update_session` tool now respects Submitter and Speakers field locks.
- **LiveBuzz** gate skip reasons now name the gate rule and the record title.
- **Maritz RTS** failed sync runs now surface the vendor's own error text and record an error count in the **Errors** column.

where.path: Multiple surfaces — Org Settings → Roles; Portals → Share login details; Account → Notifications; Embeds; Apps → LiveBuzz / Maritz RTS

entries.use_case: Organizers who bulk-send portal login details to contacts with older login emails will no longer see the whole send fail — mismatches are skipped gracefully. Admins deleting org roles can safely reassign holders without accidentally removing them from the org. Speakers and participants can now properly opt out of community emails from their account settings.

cs_action.note: All fixes are automatic; nothing needs to be enabled. The portal login-sharing fix is particularly impactful — prod had 6,453 stale login links in US and 712 in EU.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that bulk 'Share login details' fails, that deleting a role removed users from the org, or that community email opt-out doesn't work.

internal.talk_track: Several quiet reliability issues have been fixed: bulk portal login sends are more resilient, org role deletion is safer, and integration error messages are now much more descriptive.

Each page returns a stable cursor so no events are skipped on the next poll. Granting or editing a token with this scope requires the **Manage Users** org permission; the scope cannot be combined with other scopes or restricted to a single event.

A backfill script must be run per region to populate ingested_at on older ES documents.
internal.talk_track: If your security team needs to monitor who is accessing Sessionboard, what API calls are being made, and when logins succeed or fail, you can now generate a dedicated API token and point your SIEM at three log streams that page reliably with a cursor — no missed events, no manual exports.
